provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Chitin from insect/arthropod exoskeletons as bio-adsorbent for heavy metals and dyes. Second most abundant natural polysaccharide after cellulose.

mechanisms.description: Chitin amino group coordination: acetamido groups (-NHCOCH₃) and amino groups (after deacetylation to chitosan) coordinate heavy metal ions

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions and dye molecules
pollutant_feature.quote: ble coordination/chelation with various heavy metal ions

bio_structure.quote: The amine and hydroxyl groups in chitosan molecules ena-

interaction.text: Coordination with acetamido/amino groups on chitin backbone
interaction.quote: non-protonated amino groups of chitosan allow formation

why_it_works.text: Adsorption capacity varies by metal and chitin source
why_it_works.quote: improve its adsorption capacity of heavy metal ion in water

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Arthropod exoskeleton chitin provides acetamido and hydroxyl groups for pollutant binding

narrative.text: Chitin is the second most abundant natural polysaccharide, found in insect exoskeletons, crustacean shells, and fungal cell walls. It can be converted to chitosan by deacetylation, enhancing its adsorption capacity for heavy metals and dyes.

design_translation.idea: Extract chitin from insect/arthropod waste (shrimp shells, cricket exoskeletons) and use as bio-adsorbent or convert to chitosan for enhanced performance
design_translation.material_handle: Shrimp shell chitin for heavy metal adsorption
design_translation.design_principle: Chitin (poly-β-(1→4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine) provides amino and hydroxyl groups for metal ion chelation and dye adsorption
design_translation.implementation_example: Shrimp shell chitin for heavy metal adsorption; Silkworm pupa chitin for dye removal
design_translation.constraints: Chitin insolubility limits processing; deacetylation to chitosan improves adsorption but adds processing cost
material_realization_examples: Shrimp shell chitin for heavy metal adsorption
Silkworm pupa chitin for dye removal
design_translation.target_interaction: metal ion chelation and dye adsorption
